easy.def: Close to.
examples: Sit near me.
The park is near the school.
Stay near your mom.

more.def: Not far from a person, place or thing.
examples: Our house is near the beach.
A deer stood near the edge of the woods.
Please stay near me in the crowd.

easy.def: Close.
examples: The beach is near.
The nearest store is far.
Summer is near.

more.def: Not far away in space or in time.
examples: The nearest hospital is ten miles away.
The end of the school year is near.
We will move in the near future.

easy.def: Close by.
examples: A nearby store is open.
The nearby park is big.
We live in a nearby town.

more.def: Not far away.
examples: A nearby store sells milk.
The nearby park has a playground.
We stayed at a nearby hotel.

easy.def: Close to where you are.
examples: The store is nearby.
We live nearby.
A bird sat nearby.

more.def: In a place that is not far away.
examples: A friend lives nearby.
There is a stream nearby.
A cat sat nearby and watched.

easy.def: Almost.
examples: I am nearly done.
It is nearly noon.
We nearly missed the bus.

more.def: Almost, but not completely.
examples: I am nearly finished with my book.
It is nearly time for lunch.
She nearly dropped the full glass.

easy.def: Clean and in order.
examples: My room is neat.
Her writing is neat.
Put the books in a neat pile.

more.def: Clean, tidy and in good order.
examples: My desk is neat and clean.
She has neat handwriting.
The clothes were folded in neat stacks.

easy.def: Because it must be so.
examples: You do not necessarily need a coat.
Not all big dogs are necessarily mean.
It is not necessarily true.

more.def: In a way that must be true; used mostly in negative sentences.
examples: You do not necessarily need a coat, because it is warm.
Big dogs are not necessarily mean.
The most expensive toy is not necessarily the best.

easy.def: Needed.
examples: Water is necessary for life.
A coat is necessary in winter.
It is necessary to rest.

more.def: Needed in order for something to happen.
examples: Water is necessary for plants to grow.
A coat is necessary in the snow.
It is necessary to wear a helmet on a bike.

easy.def: Something you must have.
examples: Food is a necessity.
Water is a necessity.
Warm clothes are a necessity.

more.def: Something that you need and cannot live or work without.
examples: Food and water are necessities.
A warm coat is a necessity in the winter.
Out of necessity, we ate canned soup when the power went out.

easy.def: The part of your body between your head and shoulders.
examples: A giraffe has a long neck.
My neck is stiff.
He wore a scarf around his neck.

more.def: The part of the body that joins the head to the shoulders.
examples: A giraffe has a very long neck.
She wore a scarf around her neck.
The cat stretched its neck to see.

easy.def: Jewelry that you wear around your neck.
examples: She wore a necklace.
The necklace is gold.
I made a necklace.

more.def: A piece of jewelry that you wear around your neck.
examples: She wore a gold necklace.
I made a necklace out of beads.
The necklace sparkled in the light.

easy.def: A long strip of cloth that you wear around your neck.
examples: Dad wore a necktie.
A red necktie.
He tied his necktie.

more.def: A long, narrow strip of cloth that is worn around the neck and tied in a knot at the front.
examples: Dad wore a blue necktie to work.
He tied his necktie in front of the mirror.
The necktie had small white dots.

easy.def: The sweet juice in flowers that bees drink.
examples: Bees drink nectar.
The flower has nectar.
Nectar is sweet.

more.def: The sweet liquid made by flowers that bees and birds drink.
examples: Bees collect nectar to make honey.
A hummingbird sipped nectar from the red flower.
The nectar was sweet and sticky.

easy.def: To have to have something.
examples: I need water.
Plants need sun.
She needs a coat.

more.def: To require something because you cannot do well without it.
examples: Fish need clean water to stay healthy.
We needed more time to finish the puzzle.
Do you need any help with your backpack?

easy.def: A thin tool with a sharp end for sewing.
examples: Mom sewed with a needle.
The needle has a tiny hole.
I threaded the needle.

more.def: A thin, pointed tool used for sewing, with a hole for thread.
examples: Grandma threaded the needle to sew on a button.
The needle pricked my finger.
The pine tree has green needles.

easy.def: Not needed.
examples: It was a needless worry.
Needless noise.
A needless trip.

more.def: Not needed or not useful, so that it could have been avoided.
examples: It was a needless worry, since the bus came right on time.
The needless noise made it hard to hear the teacher.
They made a needless trip to the store because they had forgotten nothing.

easy.def: Having very little money or food.
examples: We gave food to needy families.
The needy kids got new coats.
They help needy people in town.

more.def: Not having enough of the things a person needs to live well, such as food, clothes or a home.
examples: Our class collected warm coats for needy children in the neighborhood.
The food drive helped many needy families in our town.
Volunteers give hot meals to needy people every Saturday.

easy.def: Bad or sad, not hopeful.
examples: Try not to be negative.
She had a negative thought.
A negative attitude does not help.

more.def: Not helpful or hopeful, and focusing on what is bad.
examples: A negative attitude can make a game less fun.
The coach tried not to give negative comments.
The test was negative, so the doctor said you were well.

easy.def: Below zero.
examples: Minus three is a negative number.
It was a negative number.
The cold day was negative five.

more.def: Less than zero, like the numbers below zero on a number line.
examples: The temperature dropped to a negative number overnight.
Negative five is smaller than zero.
On a number line, negative numbers are on the left of zero.

easy.def: To not take care of something.
examples: Do not neglect your pet.
The garden was neglected.
He neglected his homework.

more.def: To fail to look after something that needs care.
examples: Farmers must not neglect their animals.
The garden was neglected and full of weeds.
He neglected his homework and fell behind.

easy.def: To talk to reach an agreement.
examples: We negotiate the price.
The teams negotiated.
They negotiated a deal.

more.def: To talk with someone until you both agree on something.
examples: We negotiated with Mom about bedtime.
The two sides negotiated an end to the dispute.
She negotiated a better price for the bike.

easy.def: A person who lives near you.
examples: My neighbor has a big dog.
Our neighbor gave us cookies.
I wave to my neighbor.

more.def: A person who lives next to or near you.
examples: Our neighbor waters our plants when we are away.
Canada is a neighbor of the United States.
The girl who sits next to me in class is a good neighbor.

easy.def: The area around your home.
examples: I know my neighborhood.
The neighborhood is quiet.
Our neighborhood has a park.

more.def: The area near where you live, and the people who live there.
examples: Our neighborhood has a park and a library.
The whole neighborhood came to the picnic.
She walks her dog around the neighborhood.

easy.def: Next to or close by.
examples: The neighboring town.
A neighboring house.
The neighboring farm.

more.def: Located next to or near another place.
examples: We visited the neighboring town.
A neighboring farm sold us eggs.
The neighboring houses were close together.

easy.def: Not one and not the other.
examples: Neither of us was late.
I like neither.
Neither is correct.

more.def: Not the first one and not the second one.
examples: Neither of my brothers likes spinach.
I have two pens, but neither works.
Neither of us knew the answer.

easy.def: Used with "nor" to say not one and not the other.
examples: Neither Mia nor Sam was late.
It was neither hot nor cold.
He ate neither fish nor meat.

more.def: Used before the first of two choices to say that both are untrue.
examples: Neither the red bike nor the blue one has a bell.
We saw neither deer nor bears on our walk.
It is neither too hot nor too cold.

easy.def: Very bright, glowing colors.
examples: The neon sign is red.
She wore a neon shirt.
A neon sign flashed.

more.def: Very bright and glowing, like the colorful lights made of glass tubes used in signs.
examples: A neon sign flashed above the diner in bright red letters.
She wore a neon green shirt so that drivers could see her on the dark road.
The neon colors of the shop made the street look lively at night.

easy.def: A gas that glows bright in signs.
examples: Neon makes the sign glow.
The tube has neon.
Neon is a gas.

more.def: A gas that gives off a bright red-orange glow when electricity passes through it, used in lights and signs.
examples: Neon glows bright orange-red when electricity passes through the glass tube.
Many shop signs are lit with neon.
Neon is a gas that has no color or smell when it is not lit.

easy.def: The son of your brother or sister.
examples: He is my nephew.
My nephew is five.
I read to my nephew.

more.def: The son of someone's brother or sister.
examples: My nephew is learning to ride a bike.
She bought a toy for her little nephew.
Uncle Tom took his nephew fishing.

easy.def: A thin thread in your body that carries messages.
examples: A nerve sends a message to the brain.
The nerve in my tooth hurt.
Nerves help you feel.

more.def: A thin fiber in the body that carries messages between the brain and other parts.
examples: A nerve in your finger tells your brain that something is hot.
The dentist said the nerve in my tooth was sore.
Nerves help us feel pain and touch.

easy.def: Bravery.
examples: It took nerve to jump.
She had the nerve to ask.
He lost his nerve.

more.def: The courage to do something hard or scary.
examples: It took nerve to jump off the high diving board.
She had the nerve to speak in front of the class.
He lost his nerve at the top of the slide.

easy.def: A little scared or worried.
examples: I feel nervous on the first day of school.
The nervous cat hid under the bed.
I get nervous at the dentist.

more.def: Worried or a little afraid about something that is going to happen.
examples: She felt nervous before her piano recital.
He was nervous about meeting his new teacher.
The nervous horse jumped at every sound.

easy.def: In a worried way.
examples: She waited nervously.
He laughed nervously.
The dog looked nervously around.

more.def: In a way that shows you are worried or afraid.
examples: She waited nervously for her turn.
He laughed nervously before the test.
The kitten looked around nervously.

easy.def: A home that a bird makes for its eggs.
examples: The bird made a nest.
The nest is in the tree.
Three eggs are in the nest.

more.def: A place a bird builds or finds to lay eggs and raise its young.
examples: The robin built a nest in the tree.
Three blue eggs lay in the nest.
Ants and wasps also build nests.

easy.def: Strings tied together with holes in between.
examples: The fisher caught fish in a net.
The net has holes.
We hung a net.

more.def: A mesh of cords or wires tied together with spaces between, used to catch or hold things.
examples: The fisherman pulled the fish up in a net.
The soccer ball hit the back of the net.
She caught a butterfly in her net.

easy.def: A group of things that connect to each other.
examples: A road network connects the towns.
The school network is down.
A network of tunnels is under the city.

more.def: A group of lines, wires or people that are connected to each other.
examples: A network of roads connects the towns.
The school computers are on one network.
A network of tunnels runs under the city.

easy.def: Not taking sides.
examples: She stayed neutral in the fight.
The judge was neutral.
He was neutral.

more.def: Not supporting either side of an argument or fight.
examples: The referee stayed neutral and did not pick a team.
She remained neutral when her friends argued.
The neutral country did not take sides in the war.

easy.def: A plain color, like gray or tan.
examples: The walls are a neutral color.
I like neutral colors.
Her coat is neutral.

more.def: A soft color that does not stand out, such as gray, white, black or tan.
examples: The room had neutral walls so the colorful pictures stood out.
She wore a neutral coat that went with everything.
Tan and gray are neutral colors.

easy.def: Not ever, at no time.
examples: I never eat fish.
He has never seen snow.
The sun never stops shining.

more.def: At no time, or not even once.
examples: Penguins never fly, but they are excellent swimmers.
I have never been on an airplane before.
She never forgets to feed the fish.

easy.def: Even so.
examples: It was raining. Nevertheless, we went out.
He was tired. Nevertheless, he finished.
The test was hard; nevertheless, she passed.

more.def: In spite of what was just said.
examples: It was raining. Nevertheless, we went to the park.
He was tired, but nevertheless he finished the race.
The hill was steep; nevertheless, we climbed it.

easy.def: Just made, or never used before.
examples: I have new shoes.
This is a new book.
The baby is new.

more.def: Recently made or found, or not seen or used before.
examples: The school has a new playground with a long slide.
We moved to a new town last year.
Scientists found a new kind of frog in the rain forest.

easy.def: Just born.
examples: The newborn kitten is tiny.
A newborn baby sleeps a lot.
We saw a newborn lamb.

more.def: Only a few days or weeks old, having just been born.
examples: The newborn foal stood up on wobbly legs within an hour.
A newborn baby sleeps most of the day.
We tiptoed into the barn to see the newborn lambs.

easy.def: A baby that was just born.
examples: The newborn slept.
A newborn needs lots of care.
The newborn is tiny.

more.def: A baby who has just been born or is only a few weeks old.
examples: The newborn slept peacefully in its mother's arms.
A newborn needs to be fed often, even at night.
My cousin is a newborn, and she is only two weeks old.

easy.def: A person who has just arrived.
examples: The newcomer sat down.
We welcomed the newcomer.
A newcomer to our school.

more.def: A person who has just arrived in a place or has just joined a group.
examples: We welcomed the newcomer to our class.
The newcomer did not know anyone in town.
A newcomer joined our soccer team.

easy.def: Just found or just started.
examples: She has a newfound friend.
His newfound courage helped.
A newfound joy came.

more.def: Recently discovered or begun.
examples: She enjoyed her newfound freedom after school ended.
He had a newfound love of art.
The girl shared her newfound skills with her friends.

easy.def: Just now.
examples: The newly painted door is wet.
A newly hatched chick.
The newly built house.

more.def: Very recently.
examples: The newly painted door was still wet.
A newly hatched chick peeped in the nest.
The newly built house smelled of paint.

easy.def: A person who just got married.
examples: The newlyweds smiled.
A newlywed couple.
The newlyweds left.

more.def: A person who has just got married.
examples: The newlyweds waved as they drove away from the wedding.
My cousins are newlyweds and just came home from their trip.
The newlywed couple cut the cake.

easy.def: Information about something that just happened.
examples: I have good news!
We watched the news on TV.
The news made her smile.

more.def: Information about things that have just happened, in the paper, on TV or from other people.
examples: I have good news; we are going to the beach!
Mom reads the news on her phone every morning.
The news that school was closed made everyone cheer.

easy.def: A short paper with news for a group.
examples: We got the school newsletter.
The newsletter has news.
Mom read the newsletter.

more.def: A short report with news that is sent to the members of a group.
examples: The school newsletter came home on Friday.
The club's newsletter lists upcoming events.
She wrote an article for the class newsletter.

easy.def: A man who reports the news.
examples: The newsman talked.
A newsman is on TV.
The newsman wrote a story.

more.def: A man who reports or writes the news.
examples: The newsman read the evening report.
A newsman wrote a story about the storm.
The newsman interviewed the mayor.

easy.def: Printed pages of news that come out each day.
examples: Dad reads the newspaper.
The newspaper came.
The newspaper has pictures.

more.def: Large printed sheets with news, pictures and advertisements.
examples: Grandpa reads the newspaper every morning.
Our school was in the newspaper.
The newspaper arrives on our porch each day.

easy.def: A man who works for a newspaper.
examples: The newspaperman wrote a story.
A newspaperman asked questions.
The newspaperman took notes.

more.def: A man whose job is to write or edit the news for a newspaper.
examples: The newspaperman wrote a story about the town fair.
A newspaperman asked the mayor some questions.
The old newspaperman typed his story on a typewriter.

easy.def: A short old film about the news.
examples: We watched a newsreel.
The newsreel was old.
Newsreels showed the news.

more.def: A short film about current events that was shown in theaters long ago.
examples: We watched an old newsreel in history class.
Newsreels showed people the news before television.
The museum played a newsreel from 1950.

easy.def: A room where news is made for a paper or TV.
examples: The newsroom is busy.
Reporters work in the newsroom.
We saw a newsroom.

more.def: A room in a newspaper or TV station where reporters write the news.
examples: Reporters typed stories in the newsroom.
We toured the busy newsroom at the TV station.
The newsroom was full of phones.

easy.def: A small stand where papers and magazines are sold.
examples: He bought a paper at the newsstand.
The newsstand is on the corner.
Mom stopped at the newsstand.

more.def: A small stand or shop that sells newspapers, magazines and snacks.
examples: Grandpa bought a paper from the newsstand on the corner.
The newsstand sold magazines and candy.
We stopped at the newsstand before the train.

easy.def: A small animal like a lizard that lives near water.
examples: We saw a newt in the pond.
The newt is orange.
A newt swam by.

more.def: A small, slim animal with a long tail that lives in water and on land.
examples: A bright orange newt crawled over the wet leaves.
The newt hatched from an egg in the pond.
Newts breathe through their skin as well as lungs.

easy.def: Coming right after this one.
examples: Who is next?
I go next.
See you next week.

more.def: Coming right after the present one in time, order, or place.
examples: The next bus will come in ten minutes.
Turn to the next page of your book.
Our neighbors live in the next house.
